window: Free Lunch for those who RSVP
Bob Gast is a retired US Air Force officer and defense programs manager. He graduated The Ohio
State University in 1970 with a B.S. in Electrical Engineer and a commission as a
Second Lieutenant in the USAF. He graduated from pilot training one year later and
was assigned as an instructor pilot in the T-38 Talon at the 3550th Pilot Training

excerpts.line: AFB, OH he was the technical mission planner and Officer in Charge (OIC) of the technical
window: Wing, Moody AFB, GA. Later, he served as a pilot flying tactical and strategic airlift
in C-130E, C-124C and C/UC-123K aircraft.
While serving as a flight test engineer with the 4950th Test Wing at Wright-Patterson
AFB, OH he was the technical mission planner and Officer in Charge (OIC) of the technical
crew on the EC-135N Advanced Range Instrumentation Aircraft. This aircraft supported
the US space program by receiving, recording, processing and relaying in real time
the telemetry information from launch vehicles and spacecraft during their launch

excerpts.line: Later, he was named the System Program Director for the entire U-2R acquisition program,
window: on the U-2R aircraft. He then assumed program management of the advanced ground processing
station for the U-2R which generated and rapidly communicated intelligence reports
resulting from information collected by this high-altitude reconnaissance aircraft.
Later, he was named the System Program Director for the entire U-2R acquisition program,
which at that time was the number two program in the USAF ranking just behind the
development of the F-22 fighter. Bob served as an engineer and intelligence support
